rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is zero information about which modality, encoder, profile setting, or fusion strategy contributes most to validation accuracy. The entire design space is unexplored. 2) What this tests: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration—single modality, single profile, linear PCA encoder with no aggregation or fusion. It establishes a clean performance floor for the RNA signal alone, with no confounding from image features, learned encoders, multi-profile aggregation, or fusion. 3) Why it is the best first experiment: Under a limited budget, the first experiment should be fast, interpretable, and set a reference against which every subsequent design choice can be measured. PCA is computationally trivial, singleprofile avoids aggregation complexity, and rna_only isolates one modality. This baseline lets me attribute any future gain unambiguously to adding image features, a learned encoder, multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion. It also minimizes risk of a failed or ambiguous run, preserving budget for more informative follow-up comparisons (e.g., config_010 for image-only, or config_016 for the first multimodal test).

Evidence: We have only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000 → acc 0.485, F1 0.464), leaving virtually no information about whether the image modality carries any discriminative signal. The majority of the remaining search space (configs 016–051) is multimodal, so the value of that entire branch hinges on whether image features are informative at all. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image modality with a standard, well-understood encoder, giving a clean baseline for image performance without confounding from fusion, aggregation, or multiprofile. Why this is the best use of the next budget: If image_only substantially exceeds or falls below the RNA-only baseline, it immediately reshapes strategy—validating or deprioritizing the entire multimodal branch and guiding whether to invest subsequent experiments in fusion/aggregation or in improving the RNA side. No other single experiment reduces uncertainty across such a large portion of the search space.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) achieves only 20.8%, suggesting the image modality is currently very weak. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether this poor image performance is due to the weak resnet50 encoder or because the image modality simply lacks discriminative signal for this task. This experiment (image_only, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l) isolates the effect of image encoder quality by swapping resnet50 for a much stronger ViT-L while keeping everything else identical to config_010. Why it is the best next step: the result directly determines whether the image modality is worth pursuing at all. If ViT-L substantially improves image accuracy, multimodal fusion experiments become promising and worth the budget. If it remains poor, we can eliminate ~36 multimodal configurations and focus remaining budget on improving the RNA signal (multiprofile, better encoders). This single experiment maximally reduces strategic uncertainty before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile designs.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while both image-only baselines (config_010, config_013) are far weaker at ~21-23%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We have no data on whether multiprofile representation with aggregation improves over singleprofile, and no data on any aggregation method. This experiment (config_002) directly extends config_001 by switching to multiprofile + avgpool while keeping the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), cleanly isolating the effect of profile structure and aggregation. Choosing avgpool over transformer first is the simpler, more conservative test: if multiprofile+avgpool helps, we can then test transformer as a refinement; if it does not, the multiprofile structure itself is ruled out as the bottleneck, redirecting attention to encoder choice. Under a tight budget, this single-variable change from the best existing baseline maximizes information gained per experiment.

The strongest result so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) at 0.591 acc / 0.573 F1, a clear ~10.6 pp improvement over single-profile (config_001, 0.485). This confirms multi-profile aggregation is beneficial. The key remaining question within this proven design axis is whether the aggregation method itself matters: does a transformer aggregator outperform simple average pooling? config_003 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding encoder (PCA n2000), profile setting (multi), and modality (RNA-only) constant, giving a clean single-variable comparison against config_002. This is preferred over switching the RNA encoder (e.g., scvi) because it first resolves whether the aggregation architecture is a meaningful design lever; if transformer adds little over avgpool, we can rule out that dimension and focus budget on encoder choice next. Image-only results (0.208–0.227) are far below RNA, making multimodal fusion premature until the RNA pipeline is better characterized.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, while image-only models are very weak (0.208–0.227). Avgpool aggregation clearly outperforms transformer (0.591 vs 0.519). The critical open question is whether adding the image modality to the strong RNA signal provides any benefit, or whether the weak image features will dilute the RNA signal. Question tested: config_018 directly extends config_002 by adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion, keeping all other design choices identical (multi-profile, PCA n2000, avgpool). This isolates the effect of introducing the image modality. Why best next experiment: It is the single most informative comparison under budget constraints—a clean A/B test of 'best RNA setup' vs 'best RNA setup + image.' The result will determine whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion strategies (weighted, better image encoders) or to focus on improving the RNA-only pipeline (e.g., scvi/scgpt encoders). Concat is the simplest fusion, making it the appropriate first probe before committing to more complex fusion variants.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the best result so far at 0.619 acc, but only marginally (~2.8%) above the RNA-only multiprofile baseline (config_002, 0.591). Image-only performance is very weak (0.21–0.23), suggesting the image modality contributes little signal. Uncertainty: We have only tested concat fusion in the multimodal setting. It is unclear whether a weighted fusion that can learn to downweight the weak image branch would improve over the fixed equal-weight concat. Question: config_019 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted while holding all other design choices (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, multiprofile) identical to config_018, giving a clean single-variable comparison. Why best next: This is the lowest-cost, highest-information experiment available—it directly tests whether the modest image contribution can be better leveraged (or suppressed) via learned weighting, and the result will inform whether further investment in image encoders or multimodal variants is worthwhile under the limited budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder, and all completed experiments share this encoder. RNA is the dominant signal (RNA-only multiprofile avgpool: 0.591 vs. image-only: ~0.21–0.23), yet no learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200, scgpt) has been tested. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether a learned latent representation (scvi_n200) captures more discriminative structure than PCA in the multiprofile multimodal setting. Question: Does replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 improve validation accuracy when all other settings (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) are held at their best-performing values? Why this experiment: config_031 is a clean single-variable comparison against config_019 (only the RNA encoder changes), isolating the representation effect in the highest-performing regime. Because RNA drives most of the signal, a change in RNA encoder is likely to have a larger impact than changing the weak image encoder, making this the most informative use of the next budget slot. If scvi_n200 helps, we immediately identify a new best configuration; if not, we rule out a major design axis without having spent budget on more complex multimodal variants.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.678). The key evidence shows: (1) scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000 by ~4pp, (2) weighted fusion > concat, (3) avgpool > transformer, and (4) image-only results suggest imagenet_vit_l (0.227) slightly edges resnet50 (0.208). The main untested dimension in the multimodal setting is the image encoder. Config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings at their best-known values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This cleanly isolates whether a stronger pretrained image representation provides additional signal when fused with the already-strong scvi_n200 RNA features. It is the highest-value next experiment because it either extends the current best or confirms resnet50 is sufficient, reducing the search space for all subsequent image-encoder decisions.

1) Evidence/uncertainty: The current best (config_037, 0.706 acc) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l in a multimodal setting. We know scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000 in the multimodal context (0.678 vs 0.639 with resnet50), but we cannot yet tell how much of that gain comes from the RNA encoder itself versus an interaction with the image modality. The RNA-only multiprofile avgpool baseline with pca is 0.591 (config_002), but we have no RNA-only scvi_n200 counterpart. 2) What this tests: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean single-variable swap of the RNA encoder relative to config_002. It directly quantifies the isolated contribution of scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000 without the confound of image features or fusion. 3) Why it is the best next experiment: The answer strategically redirects the remaining budget. If scvi alone reaches ~0.65+, the image modality adds little and further gains should come from RNA-side improvements (e.g., scgpt). If scvi alone stays near ~0.60, the multimodal combination is essential and we should exploit the image/fusion dimensions (e.g., transformer aggregation in config_039, or scgpt in the multimodal setting). This single experiment resolves a key uncertainty that no other available configuration addresses as cleanly, making it the highest-information-per-experiment choice under the limited budget.
